question: How many links make up the complete chain of infection?
explanation: The chain of infection consists of six distinct links that must all be present for an infection to spread. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h1)

question: What happens when you successfully interrupt any single link in the chain of infection?

options.A: The infection changes into a non-communicable disease
options.B: The pathogen becomes stronger and multiplies faster
options.C: The spread of the infection stops completely
options.D: The patient develops lifelong immunity immediately

explanation: Because the chain requires every link to remain unbroken, removing or blocking even one link halts the transmission cycle. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h1)

question: What term describes the natural habitat where a pathogen lives and grows?
explanation: A reservoir provides the necessary conditions for a microorganism to survive and multiply before infecting a new host. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which of these is considered a non-living reservoir for hospital-acquired pathogens?

options.B: A nurse with an infected cut
options.D: A stray dog in the compound

explanation: Non-living reservoirs include inanimate environmental objects and surfaces like water sources, soil, and damp hospital fixtures. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h2)

question: What is a portal of exit in the spread of infection?

options.A: The medical device used to sterilize surgical instruments
options.B: The route a pathogen uses to leave the reservoir
options.C: The method nurses use to discharge a healthy patient
options.D: The medication administered to kill a causative agent

explanation: The portal of exit is the specific pathway through which a pathogen escapes its original host or reservoir. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h3)

question: A patient inhales airborne tuberculosis droplets into their lungs. What is the respiratory tract acting as in this scenario?
explanation: The respiratory tract serves as the physical doorway for the pathogen to enter the body of the new host. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h3)

question: Mosquitoes spreading the malaria parasite to a human act as which type of transmission?
explanation: Vectors are living creatures, primarily insects and animals, that transfer infectious agents from one host to another. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h4)

question: What distinguishes airborne transmission from droplet transmission?

options.A: Droplet transmission only occurs through contaminated drinking water
options.B: Airborne pathogens only spread through direct physical touching
options.C: Droplet particles remain suspended in the air for many hours
options.D: Airborne particles are smaller and remain suspended in the air longer

explanation: Airborne transmission involves tiny droplet nuclei or dust that travel long distances on air currents, unlike heavier droplets that fall quickly. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h4)

question: What defines a susceptible host in the chain of infection?

options.A: An inanimate object that harbors microbial spores
options.B: A healthcare worker who washes their hands regularly
options.C: An individual who lacks resistance to a specific pathogen
options.D: A person who has complete immunity against all bacteria

explanation: A susceptible host is someone whose immune system or physical barriers cannot successfully fight off an incoming microorganism. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why are surgical patients often considered highly susceptible hosts?

options.A: They produce too many white blood cells during operations
options.B: Their hospital diets contain excessive amounts of protective vitamins
options.C: Their natural skin and tissue barriers have been broken
options.D: They never come into contact with infectious microorganisms

explanation: Invasive surgical procedures breach the primary protective barriers of the body, making it much easier for pathogens to establish an infection. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which nursing action is most effective for interrupting the mode of transmission?

options.A: Writing accurate fluid balance chart reports
options.B: Checking the patient's temperature every morning
options.C: Performing thorough hand hygiene between patients

explanation: Hand hygiene is widely recognized as the single most effective way to prevent the transfer of pathogens from person to person. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h6)

question: How does proper sterilization of surgical instruments break the chain of infection?

options.A: It turns the operating theatre into an active human reservoir
options.B: It destroys the causative agent before it reaches a patient
options.C: It removes the susceptible host from the surgical ward
options.D: It closes off the patient's portal of entry permanently

explanation: Sterilization completely eliminates all forms of microbial life, effectively destroying the causative agent at its potential source. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h6)
